title: frankfurt contract & tender opportunities - u.s. embassy & consulates in germany
paragraphs: important! for proposals exceeding $30,000 usd (or the equivalent in local currency), offerors shall be registered in the sam (system for award management) database at https://www.sam.gov prior to submittal of their offer/proposal as prescribed under far 52.204-7 . the guidelines for entity registrations in sam are available at: sam.gov | entity registrations the website compiles standard information such as company legal name, street address, contact information, and what kind of goods and services it offers. to register in sam, an ncage code and a uei number are required. instructions for how to obtain the ncage code are available at request new ncage code (nato.int) there is no cost involved, neither in obtaining the numbers, nor in registering for sam . interested parties are strongly encouraged to register their business as soon as possible to avoid any delay in making an award to the successful bidder. failure to be registered at time of proposal submission and provide the uei as proof, may deem the offeror’s proposal to be considered non-responsible and no further consideration will be given. therefore, offerors are highly encouraged to register immediately if they are interested in submitting a response to many of our requirements. the u.s. government intends to award a contract that is the most advantageous to the government, price and other factors considered. we intend to award a contract based on initial bids, without holding discussions, although we may hold discussions with companies in the comparison range if there is a need to do so. all offerors must obtain authorization to operate and do business in germany. if hiring subcontractors , offerors must also show that all subcontractors have obtained authorization to operate in germany.  please pay attention to a crucial requirement outlined in the dosar 652.242-73 . this requirement mandates that all vendors possess the necessary licenses and permits to conduct business in germany. it is essential to ensure compliance with all german regulations and legalities to operate successfully in the country. additionally, the german tax authorities expect businesses to obtain a vat-id number and fulfill tax obligations. you should review local laws before submitting a proposal. it is essential that you have knowledge of german actuarial processes and regulations. for proposals exceeding $30,000 usd (or the equivalent in local currency), offerors shall be registered in the sam (system for award management) database at https://www.sam.gov prior to submittal of their offer/proposal as prescribed under far 52.204-7 .
the website compiles standard information such as company legal name, street address, contact information, and what kind of goods and services it offers.
to register in sam, an ncage code and a uei number are required. instructions for how to obtain the ncage code are available at request new ncage code (nato.int)

failure to be registered at time of proposal submission and provide the uei as proof, may deem the offeror’s proposal to be considered non-responsible and no further consideration will be given. therefore, offerors are highly encouraged to register immediately if they are interested in submitting a response to many of our requirements.

the u.s. government intends to award a contract that is the most advantageous to the government, price and other factors considered. we intend to award a contract based on initial bids, without holding discussions, although we may hold discussions with companies in the comparison range if there is a need to do so.

all offerors must obtain authorization to operate and do business in germany. if hiring subcontractors , offerors must also show that all subcontractors have obtained authorization to operate in germany.  please pay attention to a crucial requirement outlined in the dosar 652.242-73 .

this requirement mandates that all vendors possess the necessary licenses and permits to conduct business in germany. it is essential to ensure compliance with all german regulations and legalities to operate successfully in the country. additionally, the german tax authorities expect businesses to obtain a vat-id number and fulfill tax obligations. you should review local laws before submitting a proposal. it is essential that you have knowledge of german actuarial processes and regulations.

blanket purchase agreements (bpa’s) for services and supplies to support fra and dus consulates ****************************************************************************************************************************************************** öffentliche ausschreibung / public announcement blanket purchase agreements (bpa’s) for services and supplies to support u.s. consulates general in frankfurt and düsseldorf the u.s. consulate general frankfurt, germany invites you to submit a proposal for blanket purchase agreements to support one or both mentioned u.s. facilities. blanket purchase agreements, also known as “bpas,” are arrangements between the government and responsible sources that allow us to order supplies or non-personal services. bpas are useful for quick acquisition of items that cannot reasonably be anticipated in advance and are not available from a required source. bpas are useful when we have repetitive, but unpredictable, needs in a general class of supplies or services. a bpa is not a contract or purchase order. a bpa is like a charge account that sets forth terms and conditions prior to an actual purchase, significantly reducing paperwork and the administrative cost per order. once the bpa is issued, the u.s. government can place orders and the contractor can make delivery without a separate purchase order for each order. the exact items, quantities and delivery requirements are not known in advance and may vary considerably. bpa is not a binding contract. it is an account set up with a specific company. the u.s. government intends to renew/issue bpas for the following supplies and services: automotive services building services carpet & upholstery cleaning electrical services electrical supplies industrial and household appliances engraving equipment services engraving supplies fire protection system repair services gardening supplies glazier services hardware supplies hvac services hvac supplies janitorial services machinery repair services medical laboratory tests metal services painting services plumbing supplies personal protective clothing/ supplies shipping services steel and roof-covering services trades services waste removal services usg payment terms:  payment terms are to be 30 days after u.s. government acceptance of supplies delivered possible delivery addresses: frankfurt a.m. düsseldorf the procurement team can be reached under the following email address: e-mail: einkauf@state.gov
